meta.name: KQL Store starter pack
meta.notice: Starting points, not finished detections. Every entry needs baselining against your own estate before it is enabled as an analytics rule — read the falsePositives and tuningNotes fields on each. These have not been validated against live data in your tenant.

queries.name: Encoded PowerShell command line
queries.description: PowerShell launched with an encoded command payload. Behaviour-based: flags the use of the flag rather than any specific payload, so it survives operator retooling.
queries.query:
let lookback = 7d;
let KnownAutomation = dynamic(["ccmexec.exe", "intunemanagementextension.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-enc", "-EncodedCommand", "-e ")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownAutomation)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, DeviceId, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
falsePositives: Configuration-management agents (SCCM, Intune, Ansible) routinely use -EncodedCommand for quoting safety.
Some vendor installers wrap PowerShell in -enc.
queries.tuningNotes: Run as a hunt for two weeks and baseline InitiatingProcessFileName before promoting to an analytics rule. If volume stays high, add a per-device threshold rather than widening the exclusion list.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: LOLBin spawned by an Office application
queries.description: An Office application spawning a living-off-the-land binary. A classic macro or exploit execution chain, and rare enough in most estates to alert on directly.
falsePositives: Some line-of-business Excel add-ins legitimately shell out to rundll32.
Mail-merge and reporting automation can invoke cscript.
queries.tuningNotes: Baseline by InitiatingProcessCommandLine to find the handful of legitimate document templates, then exclude those specific documents rather than the whole parent process.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Password spray against Entra ID
queries.description: One source address failing authentication against many distinct accounts — the shape of a spray rather than a single-account brute force.
queries.query:
let lookback = 1d;
let FailureThreshold = 20;
let UserThreshold = 10;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ResultType != 0
| summarize
    FailedAttempts = count(),
    DistinctUsers = dcount(UserPrincipalName),
    Users = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 25),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by IPAddress, AppDisplayName
| where FailedAttempts > FailureThreshold and DistinctUsers > UserThreshold
| order by DistinctUsers desc
falsePositives: Corporate NAT egress concentrates many users behind one address; a stale password after a rotation then looks like a spray.
Misconfigured mail clients retry continuously with an old credential.
queries.tuningNotes: Tune UserThreshold to your largest NAT egress population. Consider excluding your own egress ranges and alerting on them separately with a much higher threshold.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Successful sign-in from an IP that just sprayed
queries.description: A successful authentication from an address that also failed against many accounts in the same window. Far higher fidelity than the spray alert alone, because it indicates the spray worked.
queries.query:
let lookback = 1d;
let SprayIPs =
    SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ResultType != 0
    | summarize DistinctUsers = dcount(UserPrincipalName) by IPAddress
    | where DistinctUsers > 10
    | project IPAddress;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ResultType == 0
| where IPAddress in (SprayIPs)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName, Location, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
falsePositives: Shared corporate egress: legitimate users succeed from the same NAT address that produced the failures.
queries.tuningNotes: This is the escalation of the spray hunt. If your estate NATs heavily, correlate on IP plus user agent, or restrict to addresses outside your published egress ranges.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: New device registered to a privileged account
queries.description: Device or MFA-method registration events. An attacker who has obtained a credential commonly registers their own authenticator to establish durable access.
queries.query:
let lookback = 7d;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where OperationName has_any ("Add registered device", "Register device", "Add security info")
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend Actor = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| where isnotempty(Actor)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, Actor, TargetResources, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
falsePositives: Ordinary onboarding and phone replacement generate this constantly.
Bulk device enrolment during a rollout will flood it.
queries.tuningNotes: On its own this is far too noisy for an alert. Join it against your privileged-role membership, or against accounts that have signed in from a new country in the same window, before enabling.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Suspicious inbox rule forwarding externally
queries.description: Creation of a mailbox rule that forwards or redirects mail. A standard business email compromise persistence and collection step.
queries.query:
let lookback = 7d;
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where Operation in~ ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule")
| extend RuleParams = tostring(Parameters)
| where RuleParams has_any ("ForwardTo", "ForwardAsAttachmentTo", "RedirectTo")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, RuleParams
| order by TimeGenerated desc
falsePositives: Users legitimately forward to a personal or delegate address, particularly before leave.
Some ticketing integrations create forwarding rules.
queries.tuningNotes: Highest fidelity when restricted to rules whose target domain is outside your tenant. Extract the target address from Parameters and compare it against your accepted domains.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Mail flagged malicious after delivery
queries.description: Messages reclassified as phish or malware after they were already delivered. The starting point for a post-delivery containment investigation: who received it and did it reach the inbox.
queries.query:
let lookback = 7d;
EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ActionType has "Phish" or ActionType has "Malware"
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryLocation
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, ActionType, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryLocation, NetworkMessageId
| order by Timestamp desc
falsePositives: Zero-hour auto purge often removes the message before a user interacts with it, so many hits need no action.
queries.tuningNotes: Pair with UrlClickEvents on the same NetworkMessageId to establish whether anyone actually clicked. Not an alerting query — this is an investigation pivot.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: User clicked a URL in a malicious message
queries.description: A user followed a link that Safe Links classified as a threat, including cases where they clicked through the warning page.
queries.query:
let lookback = 7d;
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ActionType == "ClickAllowed" or IsClickedThrough != "0"
| where ThreatTypes has_any ("Phish", "Malware")
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ThreatTypes, ActionType, IsClickedThrough, NetworkMessageId
| order by Timestamp desc
falsePositives: Security awareness training platforms generate simulated clicks that can appear here.
queries.tuningNotes: Exclude your phishing-simulation sending infrastructure by NetworkMessageId or sender domain, or the alert will fire on every training campaign.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Rare parent-child process relationship
queries.description: Parent-child process pairs that are rare relative to a two-week baseline. A stacking hunt rather than a rule — the output is a list to triage, not an alert.
queries.query:
let lookback = 7d;
let baseline = 14d;
let Common =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(baseline) .. ago(lookback))
    | summarize BaselineCount = count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName
    | where BaselineCount > 50
    | project InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| join kind=leftanti Common on InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName
| summarize Seen = count(), Devices = dcount(DeviceName), Sample = any(ProcessCommandLine)
  by InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName
| where Devices <= 3
| order by Seen asc
falsePositives: New software rollouts produce many genuinely new pairs.
Rarely used administrative tooling will always surface here.
queries.tuningNotes: Do not convert this to an analytics rule. Run it weekly, triage the top of the list, and add confirmed-benign pairs to a watchlist you exclude.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Outbound connection to a newly observed domain
queries.description: Successful outbound connections to hosts not seen in the previous 30 days, narrowed to those touched by very few devices. Newly-registered infrastructure is a strong C2 signal.
queries.query:
let lookback = 1d;
let baseline = 30d;
let Known =
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(baseline) .. ago(lookback))
    | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
    | summarize by RemoteUrl;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| join kind=leftanti Known on RemoteUrl
| summarize Connections = count(), Devices = dcount(DeviceName), Processes = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10)
  by RemoteUrl
| where Devices <= 2
| order by Connections desc
falsePositives: CDN and telemetry endpoints rotate hostnames constantly and will dominate the output.
Any newly installed software contacts new domains legitimately.
queries.tuningNotes: Expect a long tail of CDN noise; build an exclusion list of your CDN and vendor telemetry suffixes before this becomes usable. Never alert on this directly.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Scheduled task created by an unusual process
queries.description: Scheduled task creation via schtasks.exe from a parent that is not part of the normal software-management chain.
queries.query:
let lookback = 1d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe", "msiexec.exe", "services.exe", "svchost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine, DeviceId, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
falsePositives: Installers and update agents create tasks routinely.
Administrative scripts run interactively by IT staff.
queries.tuningNotes: Baseline InitiatingProcessFileName for a fortnight and extend the exclusion list to your own management stack. Consider also matching on task names written to unusual paths.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Volume shadow copy deletion
queries.description: Deletion of volume shadow copies or the backup catalogue — near-universal ransomware pre-encryption behaviour and very rarely legitimate.
queries.query:
let lookback = 1d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("delete", "shadows"))
     or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shadowcopy", "delete"))
     or (FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("delete", "catalog"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, DeviceId, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
falsePositives: Some backup products prune shadow copies as part of routine maintenance.
queries.tuningNotes: One of the few detections that justifies alerting with no baselining. If a backup product triggers it, exclude that specific product binary rather than raising the threshold.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Credential dumping tool signatures on the command line
queries.description: Command lines carrying well-known LSASS credential-dumping signatures, including the comsvcs.dll MiniDump technique that needs no dropped binary.
queries.query:
let lookback = 1d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sekurlsa", "lsadump", "minidump", "comsvcs.dll, MiniDump", "procdump")
     or (FileName =~ "rundll32.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "comsvcs" and ProcessCommandLine has "MiniDump")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, DeviceId, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
falsePositives: Incident-response and forensics tooling legitimately uses procdump against LSASS.
Some crash-reporting agents call MiniDump.
queries.tuningNotes: String-based and therefore evadable — treat as one signal among several rather than complete coverage. Pair with DeviceEvents where ActionType is a process-access event targeting lsass.exe for a behavioural view.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Azure role assignment granting privileged access
queries.description: Successful role assignment writes in Azure Resource Manager. Privilege grants are infrequent enough in most subscriptions to review individually.
queries.query:
let lookback = 7d;
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where OperationNameValue =~ "Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write"
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ "Success"
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceGroup, _ResourceId, OperationNameValue
| order by TimeGenerated desc
falsePositives: Infrastructure-as-code pipelines assign roles on every deployment.
Landing-zone automation creates assignments in bulk.
queries.tuningNotes: Exclude your deployment service principals by Caller, then review what is left. If pipelines dominate, scope the rule to assignments made by human identities only.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack

queries.name: Impossible travel between successful sign-ins
queries.description: Successful sign-ins from more than one country within four hours. A coarse proxy for impossible travel using only country granularity.
queries.query:
let lookback = 1d;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ResultType == 0
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| where isnotempty(Country)
| summarize Countries = make_set(Country), Signins = count(), First = min(TimeGenerated), Last = max(TimeGenerated)
  by UserPrincipalName
| where array_length(Countries) > 1
| extend WindowMinutes = datetime_diff("minute", Last, First)
| where WindowMinutes < 240
| order by WindowMinutes asc
falsePositives: VPN and cloud egress routinely place a user in another country.
Mobile roaming near a border produces country flapping.
queries.tuningNotes: Entra ID Protection does this properly with travel-time modelling — prefer that signal if you have the licence. This exists for estates that do not, and needs a VPN egress exclusion list to be usable.
queries.author: KQL Store starter pack
